answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to stake a costly, slow-to-earn reputation bond before it can transact. Like an onyx ledger recording every completed job, the bond grows only through verified work, so a newcomer cannot buy instant trust. A haven of high-value tasks admits only agents whose bond clears a threshold, and each deal leaves a thread linking payment, work and review. An attacker must fund and age thousands of fakes, paying real work costs for each, while one detected fraud burns the whole bond, making forgery cost more than it can steal.
